To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
people are influenced by changes that occur in a stimulus even when they fail to detect those changes.
undetected gradual changes in facial expression influence subsequent decisions about which expression was seen.

(1) people who fail to detect any change between two stimuli are nevertheless influenced by the change in their subsequent decisions, and (2), their confidence in their subsequent decisions is reduced after exposure to changing stimuli compared to exposure to static stimuli.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question: What is the relationship between the conscious experience of a stimulus and the representation of that stimulus?
the question of whether change blindness, the inability to detect changes that occur in a visual stimulus, influences subsequent behavior.
the question of how much of the information that we are exposed to in our daily lives is actually processed.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the change blindness phenomenon, in its various manifestations, is not only a failure of visual perception and attention but also a failure in the processes that follow visual perception and attention.
the undetected changes in highly salient stimulus information may be causally effective and may influence subsequent behavior.
the undetected changes in stimuli influence our subsequent behavior.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
people are not as good at detecting change as they think they are.
undetected change is not necessarily without consequence, and that the failure to notice a change in a stimulus is not necessarily the same as failing to notice a change.
people are blind to gradual changes but are not blind to the effects of these changes on subsequent behavior.
The main takeaway from our work is that
change blindness is a useful tool for studying how the brain processes visual information.
change blindness is a very powerful phenomenon that can be used to study how we process information and make decisions.
change blindness can occur in highly salience stimuli.
